systems.best_for: Research into LLM scaling laws for speech, and non-commercial zh/en cloning where the 8 B's inference-time resampling can be spent to push speaker similarity higher.
systems.watch: Two licences stack and both bite — CC BY-NC 4.0 blocks commercial use and the Llama 3.2 Community License rides underneath it. Stagnant since May 2025, with Llasa-3B down to roughly 1.2 k downloads a month.
systems.standout: Inference-time compute scaling — resample low-similarity generations against a verifier model
systems.params: 1 B, 3 B and 8 B; Llasa-3B is 4 B in BF16 tensors, built on Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct
systems.architecture: Llama LLM extended with a 65,536-entry XCodec2 speech codebook — a pure LM-scaling approach to TTS. Uniquely supports inference-time compute scaling, using a speech-understanding model as a verifier to resample low-similarity generations.
systems.codec: XCodec2 at 50 Hz (HKUST) — single-codebook semantic and acoustic unification, 65,536 entries, 50 tokens per second
systems.vram: ~16 GB for the 8 B per the corpus cloning table; not published by the authors
systems.streaming: Not documented
systems.quantisation: Standard LLM tooling applies directly — quantisation, GGUF and vLLM; 8 quantised community versions exist
systems.fine_tuning: LoRA through standard LLM tooling; 5 community finetunes published
systems.benchmarks: Llasa-8B: 0.770 SIM and 3.12 % WER on SeedTTS-EN per the corpus cloning table — the highest similarity in that table, ahead of MaskGCT's 0.728.
systems.adoption: ~1.2 k HF downloads/month on Llasa-3B — adoption has collapsed. HKUST Audio also released 160 k hours of tokenized speech as a Llama-compatible TTS foundation resource.
systems.released: Early 2025; HF card last substantively updated 2025-05-10; no 2026 activity found

systems.name: MaskGCT
systems.licence: Not established from the sources reviewed.
systems.cloning: Zero-shot from ~3 s of reference audio, with cross-lingual transfer
systems.emotion: Not established from the sources reviewed.
systems.languages_note: 6, multilingual via the Emilia corpus; zh/en are the primary evaluation languages
systems.runs_on: GPU
systems.latency_note: Not published
systems.best_for: A non-autoregressive comparison point for research, and offline zero-shot cloning where speaker similarity matters more than speed and the work is non-commercial.
systems.standout: Fully non-autoregressive masked decoding — no alignment or duration model needed
systems.params: ~1 B+ across all components; the T2S model file alone is 2.99 GB
systems.architecture: Two-stage fully non-autoregressive masked generative codec transformer — text to semantic tokens by masked prediction, then semantic to acoustic. Requires no explicit text-speech alignment and no phone-level duration prediction, which is genuinely different from every AR model in this segment.
systems.vram: The corpus disagrees with itself — ~12 GB in the cloning and deployment tables, 16–24 GB in the DGX Spark matrix
systems.streaming: None — masked generative decoding is architecturally incompatible with streaming
systems.fine_tuning: No fine-tuning support
systems.benchmarks: 0.728 SIM-O and ~2.6 % WER on SeedTTS-EN against a 0.730 ground-truth reconstruction, per the corpus cloning table; trained on 100 k hours of Emilia. The same corpus document's summary line quotes 0.777 SIM-O and the two figures do not reconcile. No RTF published. TTSDS2: MOS 3.28 ±0.14 | CMOS −0.17 ±0.17 | SMOS 4.39 ±0.14 (June 2025 (arXiv 2506.19441; SSW13, Aug 2025))
systems.adoption: ~9.5 k GitHub stars on Amphion
systems.released: October 2024; accepted at ICLR 2025. No 2026 model update.

systems.name: Echo-TTS
systems.cloning: Yes — conditioned on up to two minutes of speaker reference audio, far more than the 3–10 s norm elsewhere
systems.emotion: Implicit, carried by the long reference
systems.languages_note: English; not explicitly stated on the model card
systems.runs_on: GPU; a community app targets 12 GB VRAM
systems.latency_note: 30 seconds of audio in ~1.45 s on an A100, given a 120-second audio prompt
systems.best_for: Non-commercial high-fidelity cloning when you have plenty of reference audio — the two-minute conditioning window is what makes its speaker fidelity strong.
systems.watch: The weights are CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0: non-commercial and share-alike on derivatives, the most restrictive weights licence in this segment. Generation is capped at 30 seconds per segment despite accepting a two-minute reference, and it is a solo-maintainer project.
systems.standout: Accepts a two-minute speaker reference, far beyond the 3–10 s norm
systems.params: 2.4 B DiT
systems.architecture: Diffusion transformer generating Fish Speech S1-DAC latents, producing 44.1 kHz audio
systems.vram: ~12 GB targeted by the community EchoStudio app; not published by the author
systems.streaming: Not documented
systems.max_generation: 30 s per segment — a hard cliff
systems.benchmarks: Generates 30 seconds of audio in ~1.45 s on an A100 given a 120-second audio prompt. 44.1 kHz output. No quality benchmark published.
systems.adoption: HF downloads not tracked. Community tooling (EchoStudio) provides TTS, dubbing and cloning UIs.
systems.released: December 2025 (community tracker: 2025-12-04)

systems.name: GLM-TTS
systems.licence: Genuinely unresolved — the arXiv report carries CC BY 4.0 (which licenses the paper, not the weights) and a community tracker lists Apache-2.0; the Hugging Face weight licence could not be read
systems.cloning: Zero-shot
systems.emotion: Not documented as an explicit mechanism
systems.languages_note: 2 (Chinese and English) plus Sichuan, Cantonese, Shanghai and Taiwan Mandarin dialects
systems.runs_on: GPU; ~10 GB VRAM per the corpus cloning table
systems.latency_note: Not published
systems.best_for: zh/en work needing Chinese dialect coverage from a major lab, and as the reference point for data-efficient training — it reaches these numbers on 100 k hours where CosyVoice 3 used 1 M.
systems.watch: Nobody in the corpus could read the actual weights licence off Hugging Face. Check it yourself before building on it: the CC BY 4.0 you will find on arXiv covers the paper, not the model. No latency, no VRAM and no streaming data published either.
systems.standout: Matches CosyVoice 3 quality on 100 k training hours instead of 1 M
systems.architecture: Two-stage hybrid — a text-to-token autoregressive model followed by a token-to-waveform diffusion model. One corpus table instead describes it as LLM plus flow matching with GRPO RL; the two descriptions do not agree.
systems.vram: ~10 GB per the corpus cloning table; not published by Zhipu
systems.streaming: Not documented
systems.benchmarks: Seed-TTS-eval: 0.89 % CER Chinese, 1.91 % WER English, 76.4 speaker similarity — reached on 100 k hours of training data against CosyVoice 3's 1 M. The corpus cloning table separately reports 0.672 SIM and 2.23 % WER for English on an unnamed test set.
systems.adoption: Public demo at audio.z.ai
systems.released: arXiv 2512.14291, 2025-12-16; a community tracker lists 2025-12-11. GLM-4-Voice is a separate speech-to-speech line, not this model.

systems.name: Audio8-TTS-Preview-0.6B
systems.licence: Apache-2.0 on both code AND weights — stated in prose on the model card and the README, not merely tagged, so there is no split code-versus-weights question here.
systems.price_note: Free / self-host. No hosted API, no paid tier, no vendor pricing of any kind.
systems.cloning: Zero-shot from reference audio, but not drop-in — you must also supply a reference transcript matching the spoken content. Required clip length is published nowhere. The vendor warns that long, noisy or mis-transcribed references reduce stability and speaker similarity. It also generates with no reference voice at all.
systems.emotion: None published — no tags, no parameters, no prompt-driven style control. The only documented generation controls are temperature, top_p, top_k, do_sample and max_new_tokens.
systems.languages_note: 11, deliberately limited for the preview — Cantonese, Chinese, Dutch, English, French, German, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Polish, Spanish. Broader coverage promised for later releases.
systems.runs_on: CUDA GPU through an SGLang-Omni adapter; CPU through an official ONNX INT4 build, which is the notable path — 44.1 kHz output in roughly 1 GiB resident on an Apple M2. The vendor publishes no GPU VRAM figure at all.
systems.latency_note: Not published
systems.best_for: An Apache-2.0 reimplementation of the Fish S2 Pro dual-AR architecture at roughly an eighth of the size, with an offline CPU path — the commercially-safe way to get that design. Treat it as a prototyping and benchmarking candidate rather than a production commitment until it is older than a few weeks.
systems.watch: This is days old — weights landed 2026-07-28, the repo 2026-07-29, and the authors label it a Preview. Every star, download and SOTA claim you will read about it is launch-week material. The benchmark table is vendor-self-reported and its comparators span 1.5 B to 8.5 B; its English WER does lead that table, but its Hard-ZH CER of 11.510 is the WORST figure of every comparator with a value, and speaker similarity of 63.2% sits well below LongCat-AudioDiT (81.8%) and dots.tts (81.0%). Streaming is path-dependent: the ONNX CPU runtime streams, the SGLang serving adapter does not, so an OpenAI-compatible deployment gets no streaming today.
systems.standout: Apache-2.0 rebuild of Fish S2 Pro's dual-AR at an eighth the size, plus a CPU INT4 path
systems.params: 601.2 M (601,159,424), excluding the codec
systems.architecture: DualAR, explicitly inspired by Fish Audio S2 Pro — a Slow AR transformer (24 layers, width 896, 14 heads, 2 KV heads) predicts one semantic token per audio frame; a Fast AR transformer (4 layers, same width) predicts that frame's codec codebooks. All values read from config.json.
systems.codec: Bundled 44.1 kHz neural codec — 10 codebooks × 4,096 entries, 2,048 samples per frame (~21.5 Hz). Handles both reference encoding and waveform decoding, so no separate codec checkpoint is needed.
systems.streaming: Split by path — the ONNX CPU runtime documents streaming PCM, but the SGLang Omni serving adapter is non-streaming WAV only (also TP=1, one reference per request)
systems.max_generation: No explicit cap published. Context is 2,048 packed text+audio positions, which at ~21.5 frames/s implies an upper bound near 95 s — but text and, in the cloning path, the encoded reference share that budget, so usable output is materially shorter. Derived arithmetic, not a vendor statement.
systems.quantisation: Official ONNX INT4 build for CPU — weight-only INT4 on the AR weights, with activations, KV cache and codec staying FP16 and output FP32 at 44.1 kHz. ~572 MiB online file set.
systems.fine_tuning: Full supervised fine-tuning pipeline ships in-repo — manifest build, codec precompute, train. Single-GPU, 8-GPU and multi-node invocations documented; FREEZE_SLOW_AR / FREEZE_FAST_AR allow adapting one branch. LoRA is NOT shipped.
systems.self_host: Self-host only — there is no vendor-hosted endpoint
systems.benchmarks: Vendor self-reported. Seed-TTS: English WER 1.506% / SIM 63.2% (best EN WER in their table); Chinese CER 0.950% / SIM 73.1%; Hard ZH CER 11.510% — the worst hard-ZH figure of every comparator with a value (Fish S2 Pro 10.149, Higgs Audio v2 10.622, VoxCPM2 8.13, CosyVoice3-1.5B 5.83). CV3 multilingual error rate zh 3.205 / en 3.128.
systems.adoption: 206 GitHub stars, 21 forks; ~2.5 k HF downloads/month and 153 likes as of 2026-08-01 — all accumulated within about four days of release, and #2 trending TTS model on Hugging Face at the time of compilation. An Apple MLX conversion exists under mlx-community.
systems.released: 2026-07-28 (HF weights created); GitHub repo created 2026-07-29 — the newest model in the survey

systems.name: KaniTTS
systems.licence: Three licences stack — Apache-2.0 on the project, lfm1.0 on the kani-tts-2-en model card (inherited from the LFM2 backbone), and NVIDIA's Open Model License on the NanoCodec component
systems.cloning: Yes, via WavLM 128-dimension speaker embeddings; 3–30 s reference, 10–20 s recommended
systems.emotion: Not documented as a control surface — trained on Emilia, EmoNet-Voice and Expresso-Conversational for a conversational tone
systems.languages_note: Per-language models for en, zh, de, ar, es, ko and ja plus a 370 M six-language multilingual model; one corpus source lists only English and Portuguese variants
systems.runs_on: ~3 GB VRAM — 2.566 GB measured on an RTX 6000. Optimised for NVIDIA Blackwell; MLX build for Apple Silicon.
systems.latency_note: RTF 0.190 on an RTX 5090, 0.600 on an RTX 3060, ~0.2 on an RTX 5080 — one of the very few models publishing RTF against named consumer GPUs
systems.best_for: Consumer-GPU deployment inside a 3 GB VRAM budget with a specialist model per language, where you want per-device RTF numbers you can plan against rather than a single unqualified figure.
systems.watch: Three stacked licences, including the non-standard lfm1.0, make this genuinely hard to clear for commercial use. Cloning is the weak spot — an independent reviewer's verdict was that the TTS is fine and the cloning is not. Output is 22 kHz, and structure degrades on text longer than about 15 seconds.
systems.standout: Per-language models under 3 GB with RTF published on named consumer GPUs
systems.params: 400 M (LiquidAI LFM2-350M plus ~50 M NanoCodec); 370 M for the Japanese and MLX multilingual variants; the original KaniTTS was 370 M
systems.architecture: LiquidAI LFM2-350M backbone — 10 double-gated short-range convolution blocks plus 6 grouped-query-attention blocks, a hybrid rather than a standard transformer, claimed 2× faster CPU decode than Qwen3 — feeding NVIDIA NeMo NanoCodec
systems.codec: NVIDIA NanoCodec, 0.6 kbps FSQ at 22.05 kHz. Frame rate is reported inconsistently in the corpus: 21.5 Hz in the codec table, 12.5 fps in the validation notes.
systems.vram: ~3 GB; 2.566 GB measured on an RTX 6000
systems.streaming: OpenAI-compatible streaming API. The corpus disagrees on the rest — one source lists vLLM, MLX and LiveKit Agents integrations as shipped, the open-weights survey lists vLLM as 'coming soon'.
systems.max_generation: ~40 s (max_new_tokens 1200, configurable to 3000); structure degrades beyond roughly 15 s of text
systems.fine_tuning: Yes — KaniTTS2-Pretrain from scratch (8× H100, ~6 h on ~10 k hours of data) plus a KaniTTS-Finetune pipeline
systems.benchmarks: RTF 0.190 on an RTX 5090, 0.600 on an RTX 3060, ~0.2 on an RTX 5080; 2.566 GB VRAM measured on an RTX 6000. Trained on ~10 k hours using 8× H100 for 6 hours.
systems.adoption: 454–461 GitHub stars and ~780 HF downloads/month — very low. A community Haitian Creole finetune exists.
systems.released: KaniTTS September 2025; KaniTTS-2 February 2026 (HF collection updated 2026-02-21)

systems.name: Bark
systems.licence: MIT — relicensed from non-commercial in May 2023
systems.cloning: None official — community history prompts only
systems.emotion: Bracketed non-speech cues — [laughter], [sighs], [music] — plus MAN:/WOMAN: prefixes. It also generates music and sound effects, so it is genuinely text-to-audio rather than TTS.
systems.languages_note: 13 — en, de, es, fr, hi, it, ja, ko, pl, pt, ru, tr, zh
systems.runs_on: GPU, with smaller variants for low-VRAM devices; CPU is possible but slow
systems.latency_note: Slow — historically far from realtime; no current published figures
systems.best_for: Creative and experimental audio generation where you want sound effects and music alongside speech. A historical reference, not a production engine.
systems.watch: Abandoned since May 2023 — Suno pivoted entirely to music generation and the repo sits at 83 commits with 238 open issues and 30 open PRs. The 39.2 k stars are historical momentum, not currency, and they are the main reason newcomers still start here. Output is non-deterministic and can deviate unpredictably from the prompt.
systems.standout: Generates music and sound effects alongside speech — text-to-audio, not just TTS
systems.architecture: GPT-style transformer inspired by AudioLM and VALL-E, generating quantised EnCodec audio tokens directly from text with no phoneme intermediate
systems.codec: EnCodec (Meta) at 24 / 48 Hz — the original widely-used neural codec, now largely superseded
systems.streaming: None
systems.adoption: 39.2 k GitHub stars — still one of the highest counts in the segment. Available inside the idiap coqui-ai-TTS toolkit and TTS-WebUI.
systems.released: April 2023; last substantive updates May 2023 (2× GPU speedup, CPU offload, long-form generation, small models)

systems.name: Tortoise TTS
systems.cloning: Yes — strong multi-voice cloning from several reference clips
systems.emotion: Prompt engineering only
systems.runs_on: GPU; 4 GB VRAM achievable with optimised forks
systems.latency_note: RTF 0.25–0.3 on 4 GB VRAM with optimisations; streaming forks reach under 500 ms. Base Tortoise is famously slow — the name is the joke.
systems.best_for: Offline high-quality English cloning where speed genuinely does not matter, and as the architectural ancestor of IndexTTS, XTTS and much of the AR-TTS lineage.
systems.watch: Unmaintained upstream since roughly 2023, with 324 open issues and 24 open PRs. Use it only through a maintained fork — tortoise-tts-fast, TTS-WebUI or idiap coqui-ai-TTS. The upstream repo is a historical artefact, not a starting point.
systems.standout: The AR+diffusion ancestor of XTTS and IndexTTS; usable only through forks
systems.architecture: Autoregressive decoder feeding a diffusion decoder, with a CLVP re-ranker — the direct ancestor of IndexTTS and the XTTS lineage
systems.vram: 4 GB achievable with optimised forks
systems.streaming: Only via forks
systems.adoption: 14.9 k GitHub stars; 357 commits
systems.released: 2022; not archived, but effectively unmaintained upstream since ~2023

systems.name: Soprano TTS
systems.licence: Not established from the sources reviewed.
systems.cloning: Not documented
systems.emotion: Not documented
systems.runs_on: CPU
systems.latency_note: 1,590 ms first token to speech and a 5.7× core-hour ratio on an AMD Ryzen 7 5700X (Picovoice benchmark, 14 July 2026)
systems.best_for: Apache-2.0 on-device speech with genuine token/frame-level streaming — but only after you have measured it yourself on the hardware you intend to ship.
systems.watch: The only independently measured figures in the corpus refute the vendor's own claims. Picovoice's reproducible 14 July 2026 benchmark measured 1,590 ms to first speech and a 5.7× core-hour ratio, against vendor claims of '<250 ms' and '20× realtime on CPU' — off by roughly 6× and 30×. That benchmark is vendor-authored and Picovoice's own engine wins it, so read the framing critically, but its methodology is disclosed and the harness is public, which is more than the roundups offer.
systems.standout: The only row whose vendor claims a public reproducible benchmark actively refutes

Same run for scale: Picovoice Orca 128 ms / 0.16×, Piper 1,510 ms / 0.54×, Kokoro-82M 2,925 ms / 1.4×, KittenTTS Nano 10,670 ms / 5.1×.

systems.name: Inflect-Micro-v2
systems.cloning: None — one fixed male synthetic voice
systems.emotion: None; speed and variation controls plus deterministic seeding
systems.runs_on: CPU and CUDA — 6.28× faster than realtime on CPU, CPU model unspecified
systems.latency_note: 6.28× realtime on CPU; the CPU is not named
systems.best_for: Ultra-low-footprint deterministic English narration on CPU, where a reproducible seed matters more than having a choice of voice.
systems.watch: One fixed voice, English only, no cloning, no emotion. Every quality claim is self-reported by a solo maintainer with no track record. And despite being the #1 and #3 trending TTS models on Hugging Face they draw only ~1.4 k and ~800 downloads a month — they are trending on likes, not use.

systems.params: Inflect-Micro-v2: 9,356,513 deployable parameters (37.53 MB FP32). Inflect-Nano-v2: 3.97 M.
systems.architecture: VITS-family end-to-end text-to-waveform — English phoneme frontend, monotonic alignment, stochastic latent synthesis, residual coupling flow and an integrated alias-reduced neural waveform decoder. 24 kHz mono.
systems.streaming: Not documented; supports punctuation-aware segmentation for long text

systems.released: Inflect-Nano-v2 2026-06-25; Inflect-Micro-v2 mid-2026

systems.name: Zonos-v0.1
systems.price_note: Free / self-host; Zyphra's hosted API was $0.02 / minute
systems.cloning: Zero-shot from 5–30 s of reference audio
systems.emotion: Fine-grained controls for speaking rate, pitch and emotion
systems.languages_note: Not established from the sources reviewed.
systems.runs_on: GPU; ~6 GB VRAM per the corpus cloning table
systems.latency_note: RTF ~2× on an RTX 4090 per the corpus, which glosses the same figure as 'slower than real-time' — the ratio and the gloss contradict each other
systems.best_for: The first open-source SSM-hybrid audio model and 44 kHz native output at 1.6 B. In 2026 it is mainly of interest as the architectural predecessor to ZONOS2.
systems.watch: Superseded by ZONOS2 in June 2026, which claims 4× the throughput. Zonos-v0.1 sits at 1000 Elo, overall rank 72, in the 31 July 2026 Artificial Analysis snapshot — near the bottom of the open-weight subset. Check whether you want the predecessor at all before wiring it in.
systems.standout: First open-source Mamba2-SSM-hybrid audio model, 44 kHz native for its era
systems.params: 1.6 B, in two variants — a pure transformer and a transformer + Mamba2 SSM hybrid, the first open-source SSM hybrid audio model

systems.codec: DAC (Descript) at ~86 Hz — excellent fidelity at an expensive token budget

systems.name: Higgs Audio v2
systems.licence: Apache-2.0 on the generation model weights, with the tokenizer possibly under separate terms; the HF card lists 'other' and the backbone is Llama-derivative
systems.cloning: Zero-shot from reference audio
systems.emotion: Implicit from the text — no explicit tags or parameters
systems.languages_note: Not established from the sources reviewed.
systems.runs_on: GPU, ~18–24 GB VRAM. Boson AI claims the smallest variant runs on a Jetson Orin Nano.
systems.best_for: Offline cloning where listeners consistently prefer the output to what the published metrics suggest — GitHub reports rate it above IndexTTS 1.5, CosyVoice 2 and Chatterbox, particularly for male speakers.
systems.watch: Superseded by Higgs Audio v3, whose README explicitly tells you not to clone the v2 repo. The licence is not as clean as the comparison tables suggest — Apache-2.0 covers the generation weights, the tokenizer may not be covered, and the Llama-3.2 backbone brings its own terms. The much-quoted 75.7 % win rate is against gpt-4o-mini-tts, in the Emotions category of EmergentTTS-Eval only; the Questions category is 55.7 %.
systems.standout: Listener preference well above its published metrics, particularly for male speakers
systems.params: 5.8 B total — a 3.6 B Llama-3.2-3B LLM plus a 2.2 B DualFFN. Commonly cited as '3 B' after the backbone alone.
systems.architecture: LLM (Llama-3.2-3B) with a DualFFN head over a multi-codebook codec, trained on 10 M+ hours. A V2.5 variant condenses to 1 B via GRPO alignment and adds streaming.
systems.vram: ~18 GB per the corpus cloning table; 18–24 GB in the deployment matrix
systems.benchmarks: 75.7 % win rate against gpt-4o-mini-tts in the Emotions category of EmergentTTS-Eval, 55.7 % in the Questions category. Corpus cloning table: 0.677 SIM and 2.44 % WER for English, on a test set the table does not name.
systems.adoption: 7.9 k GitHub stars
systems.released: 2025; superseded by Higgs Audio v3 on 2026-06-04 but still published on Hugging Face

systems.name: hertz-dev
systems.cloning: None as a product feature — as a base model it continues whatever voice it is prompted with, which is implicit voice continuation rather than cloning. A corpus table rates this as 'limited'.
systems.emotion: None — implicit continuation only. Expressive patterns (pauses, inflection, breathing) come from 20 million hours of conversational audio rather than from any control surface.
systems.runs_on: Self-hosted GPU — benchmarked on a single RTX 4090
systems.latency_note: 80 ms theoretical, 120 ms measured on a single RTX 4090
systems.best_for: Research on full-duplex audio, and a permissively-licensed base to fine-tune. It is the clearest demonstration that ~120 ms conversational latency is reachable on one consumer GPU.
systems.watch: There is no text path at all — you cannot inject a prompt, a persona, or output from a separate brain LLM. It is also a base model rather than an assistant: no instruction following, no tool calling, so it needs substantial fine-tuning before it is a product. One corpus table buckets its licence as research-only against Apache-2.0 everywhere else — check the repository before you ship.
systems.standout: 120 ms full-duplex on one RTX 4090, with no text path anywhere.
systems.params: 8.5 B transformer, trained on 20 million unique hours of audio — the largest speech corpus named in this segment
systems.architecture: Native full-duplex speech-to-speech. A two-channel model processes user and bot audio simultaneously; raw audio in, raw audio out, with no text involvement anywhere in the model.
systems.codec: 8 Hz latent at 1 kbps — mono 16 kHz speech encoded to an 8 Hz representation, a lower frame rate than Moshi's 12.5 Hz and the source of the 80 ms floor
systems.vram: ~16–20 GB per the corpus tables; the 120 ms figure was measured on a single RTX 4090
systems.streaming: Bidirectional — genuine full-duplex by construction
systems.self_host: Self-host only — weights at si-pbc/hertz-dev on Hugging Face, code on GitHub. No hosted API.
systems.benchmarks: 80 ms theoretical average latency and 120 ms real-world measured on a single RTX 4090; claimed at publication to be 1.5–2× lower than the prior state of the art. No quality benchmark published — it is a base model, and task competence is not the point.
systems.released: November 2024. No successor — Standard Intelligence has not shipped a follow-up speech-to-speech base model as of 31 July 2026.

systems.name: Qwen3-Omni
systems.cloning: None — three fixed speakers: Ethan (bright male), Chelsie (warm female), Aiden (laid-back male)
systems.emotion: Not established from the sources reviewed.
systems.runs_on: Self-hosted, multi-GPU in practice; also hosted via Alibaba DashScope
systems.latency_note: 234 ms theoretical first packet (model card); ~702 ms audio-to-audio measured on Alibaba's own DashScope Realtime API
systems.best_for: Multilingual open-weights voice agents that also need vision, under a licence with genuinely no strings. The Thinker/Talker split is useful on its own — deploy Thinker as a fast speech-understanding LLM and pair it with a cheaper external TTS.
systems.watch: The VRAM is the decisive fact: the model card gives ~79 GB BF16 for 15 s of video, ~108 GB for 60 s and ~145 GB for 120 s, which is multi-GPU territory and by a wide margin the most expensive open model in this section to host. Measured latency runs about 3× the 234 ms theoretical claim. Full-duplex is not claimed — it does low-latency turn-taking and barge-in, not simultaneous listen-and-speak.
systems.standout: Ungated Apache-2.0 omni weights — but 79–145 GB to host.
systems.params: 35 B total, MoE with ~3 B active (A3B)
systems.architecture: Natively end-to-end omni-modal — text, audio, image and video in, text and speech out — via an MoE Thinker–Talker design with AuT pretraining and a multi-codebook decoder
systems.vram: Model-card BF16 figures: ~79 GB for 15 s of video, ~108 GB for 60 s, ~145 GB for 120 s. Audio-only will be lower, but no audio-only figure is published.
systems.streaming: Real-time streaming of both text and speech output; barge-in rather than genuine full-duplex
systems.self_host: Yes — Instruct, Thinking and Captioner variants all on Hugging Face under Apache-2.0 with no gating. Also served through Alibaba DashScope, whose pricing was not verified.
systems.benchmarks: Model card / paper claim a theoretical end-to-end first-packet latency of 234 ms cold-start. Independently measured in a 2026 arXiv tutorial (arXiv:2603.05413): the Thinker served via vLLM reaches 516 ms audio-to-text at 168 tok/s — hardware unstated — and the DashScope Realtime API reaches ~702 ms audio-to-audio with streaming. The gap between theoretical and measured is the useful number.
systems.released: 2025; still the current Qwen omni generation as of 31 July 2026

systems.name: GLM-4-Voice
systems.licence: Repository code Apache-2.0; model weights under a separate GLM model licence
systems.cloning: Not documented by the authors; a corpus table rates it 'limited'
systems.emotion: Not documented as a control surface; steering is via a text system prompt
systems.runs_on: Self-hosted GPU, ~18 GB bf16
systems.latency_note: ~800 ms minimum per the corpus tables; the authors publish no wall-clock figure
systems.best_for: Chinese–English bilingual open speech-to-speech, and a readable reference implementation of speech tokenisation plus flow-matching decoding.
systems.watch: Effectively unmaintained since December 2024 with no successor found — Zhipu's GLM 4.6 now turns up as a backbone inside Ultravox rather than being extended into voice. The code is Apache-2.0 but the weights carry a separate GLM model licence, so the commonly-repeated 'Apache' label is wrong for anything you would actually ship. English quality is the weak side of the bilingual pair.
systems.standout: Generation starts after 10 speech tokens; Chinese–English reference implementation.
systems.params: GLM-4-Voice-9B chat model, plus GLM-4-Voice-Tokenizer and GLM-4-Voice-Decoder
systems.codec: GLM-4-Voice-Tokenizer — Whisper encoder plus vector quantisation at 12.5 tokens per second; a flow-matching decoder on the output side
systems.vram: ~18 GB bf16 per the corpus tables; the repository publishes no figure. A --dtype int4 flag exists, implying int4 is a supported path for memory-constrained deployment.
systems.streaming: Yes — only 10 speech tokens are needed to begin generation, and end-to-end conversation needs as few as 20 tokens for synthesis
systems.quantisation: An int4 inference path is exposed via a --dtype int4 flag; no packaged GGUF/ONNX/MLX builds found
systems.self_host: Yes — weights on Hugging Face, but under the separate GLM model licence rather than the repository's Apache-2.0
systems.benchmarks: No comparable published figure. Trained on millions of hours of audio and hundreds of billions of tokens of interleaved speech-text data; notable in 2024–25 for human-like end-to-end spoken chat, and superseded on benchmarks by 2026 models.
systems.released: December 2024 (arXiv:2412.02612). No successor found as of 31 July 2026.

systems.name: Freeze-Omni
systems.licence: Custom licence — academic and research use only, not open source
systems.cloning: Not documented
systems.emotion: Not documented as a control surface; steering is via a text prompt. A corpus table rates the expressive range 'minimal'.
systems.languages_note: Not enumerated — trained on a large-scale corpus with no published language list
systems.runs_on: Self-hosted GPU — the repo recommends high-performance GPUs, CUDA and Python 3.10+
systems.latency_note: Not published — the repository breaks end-to-end latency down by component but gives no headline figure
systems.best_for: Research on adding speech to an existing text LLM without retraining it. Freezing the backbone is the cleanest published demonstration that speech training need not cost you text intelligence, and it is a template for bolting voice onto any text model you already trust.
systems.watch: You may not use it commercially. It is routinely listed as open source and one corpus licence table records it as Apache-2.0; on inspection the repository licence is academic and research use only. Nothing has shipped since November 2024, and its chunk-level duplex is weaker than the continuous duplex in Moshi or PersonaPlex.
systems.standout: Adds speech to a text LLM without touching the backbone's weights.
systems.params: 7 B — Qwen2-7B-Instruct as a frozen LLM backbone plus a streaming speech encoder and an autoregressive speech decoder; a corpus table gives ~8 B
systems.architecture: Speech-text multimodal with a FROZEN LLM — speech input and output modalities attach to a text LLM whose parameters never change during training, so no catastrophic forgetting from speech training. Duplex via chunk-level state prediction that decides whether the user is interrupting.
systems.vram: ~16–18 GB per the corpus tables; the repository publishes no figure
systems.streaming: Chunk-wise streaming input with low-latency streaming speech output
systems.self_host: Weights and inference code published, but under the academic/research-only licence — self-host is available for research, not for a product
systems.benchmarks: BigBench Audio speech reasoning 33.9% — the top open score in the corpus's comparison table, ahead of NVIDIA Nemotron VoiceChat at 29.2%
systems.released: Announced 2024-11-04; weights and inference code 2024-11-26; published at ICLR. No 2026 update found.

systems.name: VITA-Audio
systems.licence: Custom licence — academic and research use only, not open source
systems.cloning: Not documented
systems.emotion: Not documented as a control surface; steering is via a text prompt. A corpus table rates the expressive range 'minimal'.
systems.runs_on: Self-hosted GPU — PyTorch plus DeepSpeed
systems.best_for: A technique to steal rather than a product to deploy. If you are building a speech-to-speech model and first-audio-token latency is your bottleneck, MCTP is the published answer.
systems.watch: You may not use it commercially — it is widely described as open source, and one corpus licence table lists it as research-only while others quietly treat it as open. It is a research artifact with no duplex, no cloning and no tool calling, and nothing has shipped since May 2025.
systems.standout: MCTP cuts first-audio-token latency from 236 ms to 53 ms.
systems.params: 7 B
systems.architecture: Multiple Cross-modal Token Prefill (MCTP) modules enable fast interleaved cross-modal token generation — several audio tokens per LLM forward pass instead of one. Partial duplex only.
systems.vram: ~14–16 GB per the corpus tables; the repository publishes no figure
systems.streaming: Yes — designed for zero audio-token delay via hidden states
systems.self_host: Weights published, but under the academic/research-only licence — research self-host only
systems.benchmarks: First-audio-token-chunk generation cut from 236 ms to 53 ms using 32 prefill tokens, with a 3–5× overall inference speedup at 7 B scale; hardware unstated. Competitive across ASR, TTS and Spoken QA benchmarks while trained on only 200,000 hours of open-source audio, against Moshi's 7M hours and Sesame's ~1M.
systems.released: 2025-05-07; NeurIPS 2025 (arXiv:2505.03739). No 2026 update found.

systems.name: Kyutai TTS / Unmute
systems.licence: Python code MIT, Rust backend Apache-2.0, model weights CC-BY-4.0; the Unmute orchestration repo is MIT
systems.cloning: Yes — clone from any audio sample when run locally, plus a consented community voice set from Kyutai's 2025–26 Voice Donation Project. Cloning is restricted in Kyutai's own hosted demo for safety reasons.
systems.emotion: None as a control surface — voice and style are carried by the reference voice embedding
systems.languages_note: 2 (English, French) for the full stack, bounded by Kyutai STT; the TTS side covers 6
systems.runs_on: Self-host only — CUDA GPU with ≥16 GB VRAM, x86_64, Linux or WSL
systems.latency_note: TTS ~750 ms with STT, LLM and TTS sharing one L40S; ~450 ms split across separate GPUs
systems.best_for: A completely self-hosted, no-vendor voice agent on a single 16 GB GPU, with genuinely streaming STT and TTS under permissive licences — the right pick when audio must stay on-prem.
systems.watch: x86_64 Linux or WSL only: ARM64 is explicitly not planned and native Windows and macOS are unsupported. The STT choice is a trap — stt-1b-en_fr carries a 0.5 s model-level delay while stt-2.6b-en carries 2.5 s, so teams pick the bigger model for accuracy and then wonder why the agent feels slow. It is a reference implementation, not a hardened product, and being cascaded it has no true full-duplex or backchanneling.
systems.standout: A complete self-hosted STT+LLM+TTS agent on one 16 GB GPU.
systems.params: Kyutai TTS 1.6 B server model; STT stt-1b-en_fr (~1 B) and stt-2.6b-en (~2.6 B); Unmute's default in-stack LLM is Gemma 3 1B
systems.architecture: Cascaded by design — Kyutai STT → any text LLM → Kyutai TTS, glued by a WebSocket backend, with the pitch 'make any text LLM listen and speak'. Delayed Streams Modeling formalises streaming X→Y tasks with learned time-delays between streams, so synthesis can start before the full text exists and consume an LLM token stream directly.
systems.codec: Mimi, 12.5 Hz — split semantic and acoustic streams, the same codec that underpins Moshi
systems.vram: ≥16 GB CUDA GPU for the complete stack; per component LLM ~6.1 GB, STT ~2.5 GB, TTS ~5.3 GB
systems.streaming: Bidirectional — WebSocket between the browser frontend, the backend and each component server; both streaming and non-streaming TTS implementations shipped
systems.concurrency: An H100 handles ~400 simultaneous STT streams; an L40S serves 64 simultaneous STT connections at 3× realtime factor
systems.self_host: Self-host only, via Docker Compose (recommended), dockerless or Docker Swarm. PyTorch, Rust and MLX (Apple silicon) inference paths exist. Public demo at unmute.sh.
systems.benchmarks: Unmute deployment: TTS latency ~750 ms with STT, LLM and TTS sharing a single L40S, dropping to ~450 ms when split across separate GPUs — one of very few published single-GPU-versus-split-GPU comparisons in the field, and a ~300 ms co-location penalty worth budgeting for. Model-level STT delay is an explicit property: 0.5 s on stt-1b-en_fr with semantic VAD built in, 2.5 s on stt-2.6b-en.
systems.released: DSM STT/TTS released 2025; Unmute released 2025 and actively maintained into 2026

systems.name: NVIDIA Riva / Magpie TTS / Nemotron Speech
systems.variants: MagpieTTS Multilingual 357M v2607 (nvidia/magpie_tts_multilingual_357m) · Nemotron Speech ASR (nvidia/nemotron-speech-streaming-en-0.6b)
systems.licence: Both open checkpoints are under the same terms — the NVIDIA Open Model License Agreement (license_name: nvidia-open-model-license on nvidia/magpie_tts_multilingual_357m and on nvidia/nemotron-speech-streaming-en-0.6b). The Riva/NIM runtime is separate NVIDIA-proprietary software. The Magpie weights are additionally gated on Hugging Face behind a non-commercial acknowledgement — see watch.
systems.price_note: Free weights; Riva/NIM production deployment requires NVIDIA AI Enterprise licensing, unpriced
systems.cloning: None in the open weights. Zero-shot cloning was removed from magpie_tts_multilingual_357m — the model card states NVIDIA "removed zero-shot voice-cloning capability for security reasons" and lists zero-shot voice cloning under Out-of-Scope Use. The cloning-capable artefacts (Magpie TTS Zeroshot, Magpie TTS Flow) are a separate product with a different licence and no published weights; see the NVIDIA Magpie TTS Zeroshot row.
systems.emotion: Emotion-capable multi-speaker voices in Magpie Multilingual, explicit emotion mixing in RadTTS++ (beta), and SSML prosody and phoneme control across Riva TTS
systems.languages_note: 12 on both the MagpieTTS Multilingual model card and the NVIDIA TTS NIM support matrix — ar, de, en, es, fr, hi, it, ja, ko, pt, vi, zh (NIM locales en-US, es-US, fr-FR, de-DE, zh-CN, vi-VN, it-IT, hi-IN, ja-JP, ko-KR, ar-AR, pt-BR). Coverage does not differ between the open-weight and Riva/NIM paths. The narrower list on the Riva SDK TTS overview page (en-US, fr-FR, es-US/es-ES, de-DE, it-IT, zh-CN) belongs to the older FastPitch and RadTTS++ pretrained models, not to Magpie.
systems.runs_on: Self-host on NVIDIA GPUs with compute capability 8.0 or higher. The TTS NIM support matrix lists A2, A10, A16, A30, A40, A100, H100, L4, L40, GeForce RTX 40xx, GeForce RTX 50xx, Blackwell RTX 60xx and DGX Spark, all at FP16. Linux; Ubuntu 22.04 or later recommended. Riva SDK additionally covers embedded L4T (Jetson Thor, Jetson Orin).
systems.latency_note: ~500 ms server-side voice-to-voice on an RTX 5090 for the full cascade, excluding network and playout
systems.best_for: The cheapest route to sub-second voice-to-voice if you already own the silicon — a fully self-hosted cascade with no per-minute vendor anywhere in it, and the fastest published endpointing in this survey.
systems.watch: Zero-shot cloning was removed from the flagship multilingual model for security reasons, so the open weights cannot clone; a separate magpie-tts-zeroshot NIM exists but requires access approval. The licence position is contradictory on NVIDIA's own model card: the body states 'This model is ready for commercial use', while the Hugging Face access gate on the same repo requires ticking 'I agree to use this model for non-commercial use ONLY', with the gated use-case picker offering only Research, Education or Other. Get this resolved in writing with NVIDIA before shipping commercially on the open weights.
systems.standout: ~500 ms voice-to-voice on silicon you already own, no per-minute vendor.
systems.params: 364M (3.64 x 10^8), a transformer encoder-decoder with a 6-layer causal encoder, 12-layer causal decoder and a local transformer for multi-codebook refinement. The Hugging Face repo is named magpie_tts_multilingual_357m but the card states 364M for that same checkpoint — one model, not two. Nemotron Speech ASR is a NeMo checkpoint whose size was not captured.
systems.architecture: Cascaded components — Nemotron Speech ASR → your LLM → Magpie TTS. MagpieTTS generates tokens then decodes through an audio codec model, unlike FastPitch and RadTTS++ which produce mel-spectrograms for a HiFi-GAN vocoder.
systems.codec: NanoCodec, 21.5 Hz — very low bitrate (0.6 kbps) at 22 kHz output
systems.streaming: Riva TTS supports both streaming and offline inference modes, and streaming reduces latency on large requests; Nemotron Speech ASR is explicitly designed for low-latency voice-agent use
systems.self_host: Self-host the open weights natively via NeMo/PyTorch, or run Riva/NIM containers accelerated with TensorRT-LLM and Triton; NVIDIA additionally operates a hosted NIM API on build.nvidia.com that needs no local GPU, Docker or checkpoint download. The TTS NIM support matrix lists DGX Spark as a supported platform — Magpie TTS Multilingual gained DGX Spark support in Riva TTS NIM 1.10.0 (release notes 26.02.0) and Magpie TTS Zeroshot in release 26.07.0. The Riva SDK release itself targets embedded L4T (Jetson Thor, Orin); x86 data-center deployment goes through Riva NIM.
systems.ssml: SSML for prosody and phoneme control across Riva TTS
systems.multi_speaker: Multi-speaker, emotion-capable voices in Magpie Multilingual
systems.benchmarks: With Nemotron Speech ASR + Nemotron 3 Nano 30B + Magpie TTS: median time-to-final-transcription ~24 ms and ~500 ms server-side voice-to-voice on an RTX 5090 (Daily/Pipecat blog) — server-side only, excluding network and playout. Magpie TTS measures ~600 ms per sentence in batch mode on a DGX Spark and ~300 ms on an RTX 5090; Riva TTS is reported at ~100–150 ms per utterance but requires the Riva runtime stack rather than open-weight serving. Artificial Analysis blind pairwise Elo, snapshot 31 Jul 2026: NVIDIA Magpie-Multilingual 357M = 1062, overall rank 44.
systems.adoption: Distributed through NGC, build.nvidia.com and Hugging Face, and packaged by Daily as a Pipecat voice-agent reference stack; confirmed running as a complete pipeline on DGX Spark
systems.released: Nemotron Speech ASR released ~January 2026. MagpieTTS Multilingual v2607 released 2026-07-21, adding Arabic, Korean and Portuguese; v2602 covered 9 languages.

systems.name: NVIDIA Magpie TTS Zeroshot / Riva Zero Shot TTS
systems.variants: magpie-tts-zeroshot:1.2.0 (12 languages, streaming + offline) · magpie-tts-flow (en-US, offline only) · legacy Riva Zero Shot TTS beta (P-Flow, en-US, limited early access)
systems.licence: NVIDIA AI Foundation Models Community License Agreement governs use of the model; the build.nvidia.com trial endpoint is additionally governed by the NVIDIA API Trial Terms of Service. The model card states it is ready for commercial use. This is NOT the NVIDIA Open Model License that covers the open Magpie Multilingual weights — no weights are published for this model, so no weights licence exists to read.
systems.price_note: build.nvidia.com hosts it as a labelled Free Endpoint behind an Apply for Access gate; the self-hosted NIM container is access-restricted and NVIDIA publishes no price for it.
systems.cloning: Yes — this is the cloning-capable Magpie, and the reason the flagship's no-cloning headline must not be read as 'NVIDIA cannot clone'. Clones from a reference audio prompt of 3-10 seconds (aim ~5 s), mono 16-bit WAV at 22.05 kHz or higher. Pass voice Magpie-ZeroShot-Multilingual with no gender suffix plus an audio prompt; built-in Magpie-ZeroShot-Multilingual.Female and .Male are also available. Sibling Magpie TTS Flow clones for en-US, offline only. Access to both requires NVIDIA approval.
systems.emotion: The build.nvidia.com model card (magpie-tts-zeroshot v1) lists two emotions for the female voice — neutral and calm — and six for male voices — neutral, calm, happy, fearful, sad and angry. That card still describes the English-only v1; NVIDIA refreshed the built-in voices in NIM 26.07.0 without republishing an emotion list, so treat this as stale.
systems.languages_note: 12 in the NIM 26.07.0 TTS support matrix — en-US, es-US, fr-FR, de-DE, zh-CN, vi-VN, it-IT, hi-IN, ja-JP, ar-AR, pt-BR, ko-KR. Expanded from English-only in release 26.07.0. The build.nvidia.com model card is stale and still describes only English-US, European Spanish and French. Magpie TTS Flow remains en-US only.
systems.runs_on: Self-host on NVIDIA GPUs with compute capability >= 8.0 — A2, A10, A16, A30, A40, A100, H100, L4, L40, GeForce RTX 40xx, GeForce RTX 50xx, Blackwell RTX 60xx and DGX Spark, FP16 — via the NIM container. Also reachable as a hosted endpoint on build.nvidia.com with no local GPU. DGX Spark support was added for Zeroshot in release 26.07.0.
systems.best_for: Voice cloning on NVIDIA silicon once you discover the open Magpie weights cannot do it. The only Magpie artefact that still clones, and the one a buyer filtering this table for zero-shot cloning would otherwise never find — but you must apply for access first, so it is not a drop-in and cannot be evaluated on demand.
systems.watch: Access is restricted: you must be approved through NVIDIA's form before you can pull the container or use the endpoint, so this cannot be trialled on demand like the open weights. There are no open weights at all — unlike Magpie Multilingual there is no Hugging Face checkpoint, so nothing here is covered by the NVIDIA Open Model License and there is no artefact you can inspect or fine-tune. NVIDIA's own published surfaces disagree with each other: the build.nvidia.com model card describes an English-only v1 on Riva 2.19 with a T5-TTS architecture, while the Speech NIM support matrix documents 12 languages at magpie-tts-zeroshot:1.2.0. Prefer the NIM docs; the build card is stale.
systems.standout: The one Magpie that still clones — and you have to apply to get it.
systems.architecture: T5-TTS encoder-decoder transformer plus a neural audio codec, per the build.nvidia.com model card — it takes text tokens and reference audio codes as input and autoregressively predicts acoustic tokens of the target speech. Named differently from the flagship MagpieTTS architecture, though the card documents v1 and may lag container 1.2.0.
systems.codec: Low Frame Rate Speech Codec, 21 Hz, per the build.nvidia.com model card — distinct from the NanoCodec 21.5 Hz used by Magpie Multilingual. Output is mono PCM 16-bit at 22.05 kHz, 20 second maximum length.
systems.streaming: Streaming and offline inference per the NIM TTS support matrix. Magpie TTS Flow is offline only.
systems.self_host: Self-host as a NIM container, nvcr.io/nim/nvidia/magpie-tts-zeroshot, selected with NIM_TAGS_SELECTOR=name=magpie-tts-zeroshot. Access approval required before pull. Triton inference engine, Riva 2.19.0 or greater. No NeMo/PyTorch path exists because no checkpoint is published.
systems.multi_speaker: Built-in voices Magpie-ZeroShot-Multilingual.Female and Magpie-ZeroShot-Multilingual.Male, plus arbitrary cloned voices supplied at request time as an audio prompt.
systems.adoption: Distributed through build.nvidia.com as a hosted endpoint and through NGC as a restricted NIM container; not distributed on Hugging Face.
systems.released: Present as a NIM zeroshot model by Speech NIM release 26.02.0 (February 2026), English-only at that point; expanded to 12 languages with updated built-in voices in release 26.07.0 (July 2026) as magpie-tts-zeroshot:1.2.0. The legacy Riva Zero Shot TTS beta, a P-Flow model under limited early access, predates both.

systems.name: sherpa-onnx
systems.licence: Apache-2.0 for the runtime; every converted model in the zoo keeps its original licence
systems.cloning: Not established from the sources reviewed.
systems.emotion: Depends on the model served — Supertonic's inline expression tags pass through; VITS, Piper and Kokoro models have none
systems.languages_note: Not established from the sources reviewed.
systems.runs_on: Linux, macOS, Windows, Android, iOS, HarmonyOS, WebAssembly and Node.js; x86, x86_64, ARM32, aarch64 and RISC-V; Raspberry Pi, NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX, Jetson Nano B01 and Rockchip RV1126; NPU backends for Rockchip RKNN, Qualcomm QNN, Ascend and Axera
systems.latency_note: Model-dependent; the project publishes no per-board figures
systems.best_for: Shipping any of the open small TTS models to a phone, SBC, RISC-V board, NPU device or browser without writing your own runtime, and getting 12 language bindings for free. The most important deployment layer in open TTS and the one most consistently left out of comparison tables.
systems.standout: The only runtime shipping TTS to RISC-V, NPUs and 12 language bindings.
systems.params: N/A — a runtime, not a model
systems.architecture: ONNX Runtime-based C++ core with thin bindings for C++, C, Python, JavaScript, Java, C#, Kotlin, Swift, Go, Dart, Rust and Pascal
systems.self_host: Free and fully local with no internet connection required — that is the entire point of the project
systems.multi_speaker: Model-dependent. The zoo carries VCTK at 109 speakers, aishell3 at 174, a Chinese multi-speaker model up to 804, and vits-piper-en_US-libritts_r-medium at 904

systems.name: audio.cpp / audio.cpp-gguf
systems.licence: Not established from the sources reviewed.
systems.cloning: Depends on the model served
systems.emotion: Depends on the model served
systems.languages_note: Not established from the sources reviewed.
systems.runs_on: CPU-first via GGUF quantisation
systems.best_for: Running large TTS models quantised on CPU — Voxtral 4B fits in 7.43 GB at Q4_K. The emerging GGUF story for speech, and the closest thing the segment has to what llama.cpp did for text.
systems.standout: GGUF for speech — a 4 B TTS model in 7.43 GB.
systems.params: N/A — a quantisation stack and model collection, not a model
systems.architecture: A llama.cpp analogue for audio models, with native GGUF conversions
systems.streaming: Not documented
systems.self_host: Self-host only — there is no hosted service

systems.name: ExecuTorch (PyTorch Edge)
systems.licence: Not established from the sources reviewed.
systems.cloning: Depends on the model served
systems.emotion: Depends on the model served
systems.languages_note: Determined by the exported model. The only speech models in the official set are Voxtral Realtime and Voxtral TTS — there is no ExecuTorch-official Piper, Kokoro or Supertonic export path documented.
systems.runs_on: Smartphones down to microcontrollers — a ~50 KB core runtime with 12+ hardware backends. Cortex-M was promoted to a first-class embedded target in v1.2.0 with CMSIS-NN accelerated kernels; CUDA and Metal GPU backends arrived in v1.1.0, and Arm, CUDA, Metal and Vulkan improved across v1.3.x.
systems.best_for: Shipping PyTorch-authored speech models to phones and microcontrollers with a tiny runtime — the only mainstream path from PyTorch straight to a Cortex-M class device.
systems.watch: TTS support in the official model set is thin, and no TTS model is documented as running on the Cortex-M backend at all — so the headline embedded story does not yet reach speech synthesis. Export and quantisation work is non-trivial, and for most on-device TTS you will still reach for ONNX Runtime or sherpa-onnx instead.
systems.standout: The only PyTorch-to-microcontroller path — though not yet for TTS.
systems.params: N/A — a runtime, not a model
systems.architecture: Ahead-of-time export to .pte plus a small C++ runtime with delegated backends
systems.streaming: Yes for Voxtral Realtime, with streaming fixes in v1.3.1
systems.self_host: Self-host only — an export toolchain and runtime you build into your own application
systems.released: v1.0.0, v1.1.0, v1.2.0 and v1.3.1 are the recent line. The project's own release dates could not be reliably extracted and are deliberately not reproduced here. v1.2.0 added Voxtral Realtime, NVIDIA NeMo Sortformer diarisation and Silero VAD, promoted Cortex-M to first-class and cut 10–15 KB from the core runtime binary; v1.3.1 added Voxtral TTS improvements.

systems.name: ONNX Runtime Web / Transformers.js
systems.licence: Transformers.js Apache-2.0, ONNX Runtime Web MIT; model licences vary
systems.cloning: Depends on the model served — OuteTTS clones from a reference speaker; Kokoro and SpeechT5 do not, SpeechT5 using fixed speaker embeddings instead
systems.emotion: Depends on the model served — none for Kokoro or SpeechT5
systems.languages_note: Determined by the model. The TTS models with working browser paths are Kokoro-82M via kokoro-js, SpeechT5 via Xenova/speecht5_tts, OuteTTS via a WebGPU demo, and Supertonic, which ships its own WebGPU browser runtime. sherpa-onnx also builds to WebAssembly for browser TTS.
systems.runs_on: Any browser with WebAssembly; WebGPU acceleration by setting device 'webgpu' — broadly available on Chrome and Edge, uneven on Safari and Firefox. Also Node.js on CPU.
systems.latency_note: No published cross-browser figures. Hugging Face states that with WebGPU models 'should easily have realtime generation on the web' — a vendor claim with no conditions attached.
systems.best_for: Genuinely private, zero-server browser TTS at modern model quality — the only way to get Kokoro-class output in a web page without an API call.
systems.watch: Model download is the whole story. The smallest useful Kokoro build is 86 MB at q8f16 and fp32 is 326 MB, which is a hard first-load cost and a caching problem on mobile. WebGPU can silently fall back to WASM at a large speed penalty, and iOS Safari memory limits will kill larger models.
systems.standout: Kokoro-class TTS in a web page, no server and no API call.
systems.params: N/A — a runtime, not a model
systems.architecture: ONNX models executed by onnxruntime-web over WASM SIMD with threads, or via WebGPU/WebNN
systems.streaming: Model-dependent — kokoro-js and the community StreamingKokoroJS project do chunked streaming; the runtime itself has no token-level streaming primitive
systems.quantisation: Kokoro ONNX dtypes exposed through kokoro-js — fp32 326 MB, fp16 163 MB, q8 92.4 MB, q8f16 86 MB, q4 305 MB, q4f16 154 MB
systems.self_host: Runs entirely in the user's browser — no server, no API call and no text leaving the device, which is the strongest privacy position in the segment
systems.released: Continuously updated through 2026

systems.name: MLX / mlx-audio
systems.cloning: Depends on the model served — supported for Qwen3-TTS, CSM, Chatterbox and Marvis
systems.emotion: Depends on the model served — Chatterbox reaction tags, for example
systems.languages_note: Determined by the model. The supported set includes Kokoro (54 voices, multilingual), Qwen3-TTS, OmniVoice (claimed 646+ languages), KugelAudio (24 European languages), Voxtral (20 voices), Ming Omni TTS, LongCat-AudioDiT, MOSS-TTS variants, Higgs Audio v3, CSM/MisoTTS, KittenTTS, Dia, OuteTTS, Spark, Chatterbox and Soprano.
systems.runs_on: Apple Silicon Macs (M1, M2, M3, M4) only, Python 3.10+; ffmpeg is needed only for MP3, FLAC and OGG output, WAV works without it
systems.best_for: The fastest path to running 20+ modern TTS models natively on a Mac with unified-memory GPU acceleration and aggressive quantisation, behind an OpenAI-compatible REST API that drops into existing tooling.
systems.watch: Apple Silicon only — there is no Linux, Windows, Android or iOS path, so nothing you build on it ports to a phone or an SBC. No benchmark numbers are published in the repo at all, and support quality varies widely because many entries are community conversions.
systems.standout: 20+ TTS models on a Mac behind an OpenAI-compatible REST API.
systems.params: N/A — a runtime, not a model
systems.architecture: MLX-native inference layer plus per-model implementations; mlx-community hosts the pre-converted weights
systems.streaming: Yes — audio is generated as a stream during inference
systems.quantisation: 3-, 4-, 6- and 8-bit, plus MXFP4, MXFP8 and NVFP4. Kokoro is offered in bf16 and 8-, 6- and 4-bit.
systems.self_host: Self-host only, on your own Mac; ships a web UI alongside the REST API
systems.released: Actively developed through 2026

systems.name: Amphion Vevo
systems.licence: Code MIT (Amphion repo); WEIGHTS CC-BY-NC-4.0 — non-commercial
systems.cloning: Zero-shot voice imitation from a short reference clip
systems.emotion: Timbre and style are independently controllable — you decide separately whether the source's speaking style and accent travel with the voice
systems.languages_note: Cross-lingual conversion including accent transfer; no language count published
systems.runs_on: 8–12 GB VRAM
systems.latency_note: Not published
systems.best_for: Cross-lingual voice conversion and accent control — converting accented speech into a target speaker while choosing independently whether the accent comes along. Nothing else in this section separates timbre from style explicitly.
systems.standout: The only converter separating timbre from style, so accent travel is optional.
systems.architecture: Controllable voice imitation with independently controllable timbre and style
systems.self_host: Self-host only. No hosted service appears in the corpus.
systems.released: Vevo was published at ICLR 2025 and released in Amphion 2024-12-22.

systems.name: Amphion Vevo2
systems.licence: Code MIT (Amphion repo); WEIGHTS CC-BY-NC-ND-4.0 — non-commercial AND no derivatives
systems.cloning: Zero-shot from a reference clip, for speech and for singing; timbre is disentangled from content and style
systems.emotion: Prosody, style and timbre are separately controllable. A music-notation-free prosody tokenizer lifts melody and prosody from speech, singing or even instrumental audio, so melody control needs no score.
systems.languages_note: Model card declares six — English, Chinese, Japanese, Korean, German, French (the Emilia-101k languages). The paper evaluates English and Chinese only.
systems.runs_on: Not established from the sources reviewed.
systems.best_for: Singing as a first-class output. Text-to-singing, singing voice synthesis, singing voice conversion, singing style conversion, and humming- or instrument-to-singing, alongside ordinary zero-shot TTS and voice conversion — all from one checkpoint.
systems.watch: The weights are CC-BY-NC-ND-4.0, stricter than Vevo's CC-BY-NC-4.0. NoDerivatives means you may redistribute the checkpoint unmodified but are not granted the right to publish a fine-tune or adaptation. The MIT licence on the Amphion repo covers the code only and grants nothing over the weights.
systems.standout: Speech and singing from one checkpoint — and weights that forbid derivatives.
systems.params: 509 M AR (Qwen2.5-0.5B init) + 363 M flow-matching transformer + 255 M Vocos-based vocoder
systems.architecture: Two stages: autoregressive content-style modelling for text/prosody/style control, then flow-matching acoustic modelling for timbre control
systems.codec: Two VQ-VAE tokenizers — prosody, 512-entry codebook at 6.25 Hz (56.25 bps); content-style, 16,384-entry codebook at 12.5 Hz (175 bps)
systems.self_host: Self-host only. No hosted service published.
systems.adoption: Trained on Emilia-101k (~101k h speech) plus SingNet-7k (~7k h singing voice)
systems.released: Released in Amphion 2026-03-25. Paper arXiv:2508.16332 (v1 August 2025, v3 March 2026), accepted by IEEE TASLP.

corrections.claim: A model's arena rank is a property of the model, so one leaderboard is enough.
corrections.reality: The two largest public speech arenas disagree sharply on the same named model. Kokoro-82M scores 1479 on TTS Arena V2 and 1055 on Artificial Analysis; ElevenLabs v3 is rank 10 of 92 on Artificial Analysis and roughly 28th on TTS Arena V2. The scales are not comparable either — one is Bradley-Terry strength centred on 1500, the other an LMSYS-style Elo regression. Quote a rank only with the board and the date attached; the Rating column here is Artificial Analysis alone, for that reason.

corrections.claim: Low word error rate means a model sounds good.
corrections.reality: WER correlates NEGATIVELY with perceived quality — rho -0.11 to -0.45 across ~11,800 human ratings. Over-articulated, recogniser-friendly speech scores well on WER and sounds worse to a listener. Any ranking built on Seed-TTS-eval WER is measuring intelligibility to a machine, not quality to a person.

corrections.claim: Azure standard neural TTS is $16 per 1M characters
corrections.reality: $15.00, consistently across 35 commercial regions per the retail price API, and $18.75 in Azure Government.

corrections.claim: Azure Neural HD is $30 per 1M characters
corrections.reality: $22.00 since March 2026 — which makes Azure HD cheaper than Google Chirp 3 HD and Amazon Polly Generative.

corrections.claim: Fish Audio S2 Pro is MIT-licensed
corrections.reality: It is the Fish Audio Research License, which is non-commercial. Fish's own blog says "open weights, not open source by the OSI definition".

corrections.claim: IndexTTS 2 is Apache-2.0
corrections.reality: A custom bilibili Model Use License with MAU and revenue thresholds, prohibited-use clauses, and PRC governing law.

corrections.claim: F5-TTS is MIT
corrections.reality: The code is MIT; the released checkpoints are CC-BY-NC because of the Emilia training corpus.

corrections.claim: OuteTTS is Apache-2.0
corrections.reality: The model card's own front-matter says CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0 — non-commercial and share-alike.

corrections.claim: Piper is MIT-licensed
corrections.reality: GPL-3.0 since v1.3.0. The MIT-era repository has been archived read-only since October 2025.

corrections.claim: MegaTTS 3 is Apache-2.0 and does voice cloning
corrections.reality: Apache-2.0 in name only — the WaveVAE encoder is withheld, so you cannot encode your own reference audio.

corrections.claim: PlayHT is a leading TTS vendor
corrections.reality: Permanently shut down on 31 December 2025. All customer voice clones were deleted with no export path.

corrections.claim: Replica Studios is the SAG-AFTRA-approved AI voice vendor
corrections.reality: Ceased operations. Its site serves a farewell notice and its pricing page returns 404.

corrections.claim: Papercup competes with ElevenLabs on dubbing
corrections.reality: Acquired — papercup.com now redirects to RWS.

corrections.claim: VocaliD is a voice-banking option
corrections.reality: Absorbed — vocalid.ai redirects to Veritone Voice, with no mention of the brand.

corrections.claim: ACX accepts AI narration
corrections.reality: ACX's own requirements state unauthorised text-to-speech is prohibited. The only sanctioned paths are Amazon Virtual Voice and an invite-only ACX beta.

corrections.claim: Gemini Nano will handle on-device TTS on Android
corrections.reality: It will not. The on-device audio tasks are speech RECOGNITION, not generation.

corrections.claim: KittenTTS is fast because it is only 25 MB
corrections.reality: An open benchmark measured it at 5.1× slower than realtime — among the slowest engines tested.

corrections.claim: Lower word error rate means better TTS
corrections.reality: WER correlates NEGATIVELY with perceived quality across ~11,800 human ratings. Over-articulated, flat, recogniser-friendly speech scores well and sounds bad.

corrections.claim: Freeze-Omni and VITA-Audio are open source
corrections.reality: Both carry custom academic and research-only licences prohibiting commercial use.

corrections.claim: The EU AI Act was delayed
corrections.reality: Only the high-risk deadlines moved. Article 50 transparency applied from 2 August 2026 as originally scheduled.

corrections.claim: The NO FAKES Act is law
corrections.reality: It cleared Senate Judiciary in June 2026 but has passed neither chamber. Treat "NO FAKES compliant" as marketing.

corrections.claim: Anthropic has a TTS API
corrections.reality: It has no TTS, no speech-to-speech model and no audio output modality of any kind.

gaps: Data retention and training-on-your-data policy could not be verified from primary sources for most vendors. TTS inputs routinely contain personal data — get these terms contractually.

Tencent, Baidu and Yandex pricing is unverifiable from English-language primary sources. Tencent publishes no rate and its billing docs 404; Baidu's pricing page returns empty content; Yandex's docs sit behind a bot-check.
MiniMax Speech 2.6 pricing is reported at $60–100 per million characters by third parties, and no MiniMax-owned page would confirm it. It is therefore omitted rather than published as fact.
Amazon Nova 2 Sonic language coverage, voice list, latency and regional availability could not be reached. Do not assume it inherits v1's five-language list.
Latency for almost every hyperscaler is simply not published. Microsoft is the only one stating a concrete figure, so every latency comparison in that segment rests on third-party measurement.
Essentially no vendor publishes quality metrics — MOS, UTMOS, WER or arena rating — for its 2026 voice sets.
Per-service compliance certifications (HIPAA BAA eligibility, FedRAMP level, GDPR DPA specifics) were not verified per TTS product. Regulated procurement must confirm directly.
No watermark robustness figure in circulation is a verified benchmark. Vendor accuracy claims for audio watermarking do not appear in the corresponding repositories.
Several licences remain genuinely ambiguous — ZONOS2, GLM-TTS weights, NeuTTS Nano, MaskGCT checkpoints, and KaniTTS's three stacked licences.
